name: OSINT — People, Infrastructure & Metadata
tagline: Passive intelligence on people, exposed infrastructure, and document metadata — for authorized recon and for auditing your own digital footprint.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.desc: Checks a username across 400+ social networks using HTTP status/pattern heuristics; the most widely maintained CLI for username existence.
tools.when: Find every public profile tied to a username you own, or verify a handle before cleaning up your own exposure.

tools.name: Maigret
tools.desc: Collects a username dossier across 3000+ sites, tagging each account by type (social, dating, code) and generating HTML/PDF/JSON reports; actively maintained with a frequently refreshed site database.
tools.when: When Sherlock's pass/fail list is not enough and you want account tags, graph export, and a readable report of where a username appears.

tools.name: WhatsMyName
tools.desc: A community-maintained JSON dataset covering 700+ sites with exact success/not-found detections; the data layer behind many username checkers and the whatsmyname.app web UI since the bundled checker scripts were removed in 2023.
tools.when: When you want the raw detection data to audit a check result or drive your own checker against a curated site list.

tools.name: namechk
tools.desc: Free web service that checks a name across 100+ social platforms and 36 domain extensions in one view; a hosted service, not a self-hosted tool — no API and no bulk mode.
tools.when: A quick browser-only triage of where a name is already taken before you invest in CLI pipelines.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.desc: Passively harvests emails, employee names, subdomains, hosts, and API leaks for a domain from open sources; the reference OSINT email/subdomain harvester, actively maintained.
tools.when: Map every email address and subdomain publicly linked to a domain you own before hardening mail and DNS.

tools.name: Holehe
tools.desc: Checks whether an email is registered on 120+ sites by replaying their password-recovery flows without sending anything to the mailbox, so the target address is not alerted.
tools.when: Find which platforms a leaked or owned email is tied to so you can spot stale accounts you control that still need securing.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.desc: Framework for phone OSINT: country, area, carrier, line type, and footprint lookups via configurable scanners; stable but no longer actively maintained, so expect scanners to drift over time.
tools.when: Resolve a phone number you own or are authorized to analyze into provider/line-type facts before deeper carrier-level checks.

tools.name: emailrep.io
tools.desc: Hosted API/service that scores an email's reputation, flags breach exposure and disposable/spammy providers, and lists the online profiles tied to it; a service, not a tool — the free tier needs no key, higher limits need one.
tools.when: Triage a suspicious inbound email or audit your own addresses for exposure as part of defensive OSINT.

tools.name: Instaloader
tools.desc: Downloads Instagram profiles, posts, hashtags, highlight stories, and companion metadata (captions, likes, comments) via its own private API without an official key; actively maintained and scriptable.
tools.when: Pull an archive of a public profile you own for media/evidence preservation, or collect hashtag and post metadata on your own accounts.

tools.name: snscrape
tools.desc: Python CLI/library that scrapes public posts and profiles from several platforms with JSONL output; Twitter/X scrapers are dead behind the login wall and Reddit needs the closed Pushshift, but Telegram, Weibo, and some Mastodon instances still work.
tools.when: Programmatic bulk retrieval and archiving of public posts from the platforms snscrape still supports, e.g. Telegram channels.

tools.name: OSINTgram
tools.desc: Interactive shell that collects public Instagram data — profile info, captions, followers, tagged users, comments, and bio contact strings — using a scratch-account session or a free HikerAPI token; the project's own disclaimer limits use to educational/authorized targets.
tools.when: Relationship analysis of a public profile you own (who comments, who is tagged, contact strings in bios).
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/Datalux/Osintgram && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Shodan
tools.desc: The reference internet device/port search engine indexing exposed services, banners, vulnerabilities, and history for any IP or domain; a commercial service with a lasting free tier and a separate no-key InternetDB lookup endpoint.
tools.when: See every port and service your public IP ranges expose right now, exactly as an attacker would, before closing them.

tools.name: Censys
tools.desc: Internet-wide scan platform covering hosts, services, certificates, and web properties with structured query language; the free tier includes search plus host/cert/web-property lookup APIs.
tools.when: Certificate-centric inventory and pivots — find every host presenting a given cert — or structured queries beyond Shodan's free tier.

tools.name: ZoomEye
tools.desc: Cyber-space search engine by KnownSec scanning IPv4/IPv6, services, and web layers via Xmap/Wmap; strongest on IoT/OT devices and Asian-region asset coverage, with roughly 10k free API queries/month.
tools.when: Coverage of less-Shodanized regions or internet-of-things/embedded device hunting on ranges you own.

tools.name: Netlas
tools.desc: Internet scanning platform over 8B+ indexed hosts with response-body, DNS, WHOIS, and certificate search plus a full REST API and Python SDK; the free tier is key-limited at about 50 requests/day.
tools.when: Regular-expression/Lucene search across full HTTP response bodies when Shodan's banners are too shallow.

tools.name: exiftool
tools.desc: Reads, writes, and edits EXIF/GPS/IPTC/XMP and hundreds of tag formats across images, PDFs, Office files, and more; the metadata workhorse behind most doc-forensics pipelines.
tools.when: Forensic-grade tag extraction from any local file — geolocation, author, generator, timestamps — before release or after acquisition.

tools.name: Metagoofil
tools.desc: Dork-driven document harvesting: finds indexed files (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx) on a domain and downloads them for stripping; the maintained opsdisk fork ships on Kali and deliberately defers metadata analysis to exiftool.
tools.when: Collect every publicly indexed document on a domain you own so you can scrub metadata and accidental information leaks.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/opsdisk/metagoofil && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: FOCA
tools.desc: Windows GUI (C# with a SQL Server back end) that searches a domain via Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo, fingerprints documents, and extracts metadata — users, folders, software — into a browsable project; a Windows GUI, not a POSIX tool, with slow updates.
tools.when: When you have a Windows box and want a point-and-click metadata project view instead of CLI pipelines.

tools.name: SpiderFoot
tools.desc: Automated OSINT correlation engine with 200+ modules and a YAML correlation engine, surfaced through a web UI and CLI; built to map an attack surface and connect entities automatically.
tools.when: A broad sweep of a domain/IP/email you own to correlate entities across many free data sources in a single scan.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/smicallef/spiderfoot && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Maltego
tools.desc: Commercial graph-based link-analysis and OSINT platform (desktop and browser) with transforms into 1B+ identities, breach data, and infrastructure datasets; a free Community Edition (Basic plan) exists but is result-limited. A commercial service, not open source.
tools.when: Investigative link analysis where a visual graph of who/what connects to whom beats JSON output.
tools.install: preinstalled (web/desktop — free CE with Maltego ID)

tools.name: recon-ng
tools.desc: Metasploit-style modular reconnaissance framework for web OSINT, with a marketplace of modules, workspace isolation, and database-backed reporting; stable but leisurely maintained.
tools.when: Scripted, repeatable recon workflows with structured output and API keys for your own estate.

tools.name: Google Hacking Database (GHDB)
tools.desc: Reference catalog of search-engine operators ('dorks') and example queries that surface exposed files, login panels, admin pages, and misconfigurations in public indexes. A reference page, not a tool.
tools.when: Compose and reuse proven search-engine queries to audit what public indexes expose about your own domains.
